evidence.field: 形義源流通解; 甲骨、金文用例
evidence.text: The database analyzes early 新 as 斤 (axe) plus 辛, with 辛 also serving as a sound component; some forms add 木, sharing strokes with 辛. It reports a Shang oracle-bone example, 《合集》30973, 新鬯 (‘newly brewed wine’), and later bronze uses including 新邑 and 新君. Thus the attested oracle-bone use already includes ‘new’; the sequence ‘firewood first, then borrowed for new’ is an etymological interpretation, not a chronology established by these examples. The account also records a proposal that 新 is an expanded form of 𣓀, whose graph is interpreted as splitting wood with a wedge.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：新

evidence.source: 《說文解字》 online text and 段玉裁注
evidence.text: The received Shuowen entry says ‘取木也。从斤新聲’ (‘taking wood; from 斤, with 新 as phonetic’). Duan Yucai argues the text should instead be read ‘从斤木，辛聲’ (‘from 斤 and 木, 辛 as phonetic’), rejecting the received component analysis. Shuowen is an early historical account of the graph, but its component wording conflicts with later paleographic analysis and is not independent proof of the graph’s origin.
evidence.title: 說文解字「新」

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese University of Hong Kong)
evidence.text: Records the received Shuowen form ‘从斤，(新)[𣓀]聲’ and contrasts it with the analysis of early forms as 斤+辛, sometimes with an added 木. It says the latter represents chopping wood for fuel, and interprets 薪 as later marked with 艸 after 新 was used for ‘new’. The dossier’s alternatives therefore remain: a firewood graph later used for ‘new’; an analysis of 新 as an expanded 𣓀; and Shuowen/Duan’s differing phonetic-component accounts. The object-name and original pronunciation of any depicted chopping implement are not independently established by the cited material.

gaps: No verified official Unihan record was accessible for 新; no supplied local reading row was provided for 辛 or 薪, so their current Mandarin readings were not independently cross-checked here. The local 新 row reports kMandarin xīn and Baxter–Sagart MC sin / OC *s.tsʰi[n].

The phonetic component 辛 is identified by CUHK as a sound component, but this search did not retrieve its exact historical reading row in the same reconstruction system; an independently sourced component-to-host historical comparison remains incomplete.

The firewood interpretation and borrowing account are not fully resolved: CUHK reports both the firewood analysis and oracle-bone use of 新 for ‘new’. No dated early attestation of the standalone spoken word for firewood, no exact borrowing date, and no independent reconstruction of the depicted tool’s name/pronunciation were verified. The ‘phonetic loan’ account should therefore be framed as an analysis, not a directly demonstrated sound borrowing chronology.
No glyph image was visually inspected. The dossier’s local seal-script image lead was not investigated, so no claims are made about that specimen’s provenance or graphic details.
Modern reading/source page access limits: the official Unicode endpoint could not be fetched; local data is reported as local evidence only.

The pronunciation of the depicted wood-splitting implement is not independently established. A reconstruction for 新 alone would not establish the implement's name or prove a whole-graph loan based on that name.

The firewood-first and loan-to-‘new’ account remains an etymological interpretation: the reported oracle-bone 《合集》30973 use already means ‘new’, and no earlier dated attestation of a standalone firewood word or exact loan date was verified.

CUHK identifies 辛 as a phonetic component, but this research did not retrieve a reliable same-system historical reading row for 辛. The local Baxter–Sagart 新 row is supplied, but no local 辛 row was supplied; the modern xīn match does not establish ancient phonetic history.
No exact contemporary artifact photo or independently dated first appearance of the graph was retrieved; selected Commons images are labeled script-style redrawings with database/source-image leads.

The official Unihan endpoints for both 新 and 辛 could not be opened in the web tool. The local 新 reading is retained with local provenance only; 辛’s kMandarin xīn is supported here by a third-party Unihan-rendering page.
